speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly when the baby started having bilious vomiting and if they've passed any stool since birth? Also, was the mother's pregnancy or the delivery process complicated in any way?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the infant had any fever or signs of respiratory distress, and has the mother noticed any blood in the stool or vomit? I also need to know if the infant is feeding well and how much weight they have gained or lost since birth.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Inability to pass meconium, Abdominal distension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the infant have a family history of cystic fibrosis, and has a rectal exam been performed to check for a palpable mass or the absence of stool? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal X-Ray Findings: Dilated loops of bowel with no gas in the rectum, suggestive of a distal obstruction. Rectal Biopsy Histopathology: Absence of ganglion cells in the submucosa and myenteric plexus, consistent with Hirschsprung’s disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung’s Disease

The rectal biopsy confirming the absence of ganglion cells, combined with the clinical presentation of bilious vomiting and failure to pass meconium, definitively diagnoses Hirschsprung’s disease. We will immediately arrange for surgical consultation to correct the obstruction.
